title: Svartsengi GNSS uplift in 2023-2026: trigger rules that timed ten earlier Icelandic intrusions and eruptions best predicted an event by early 2026 that did not occur, while steady recharge continued
abstract: Question: from November 2023 to July 2025 the Svartsengi magma reservoir (Reykjanes, Iceland) fed two intrusions and nine eruptions; after July 2025 the ground rose for more than 15 months without an event. Which trigger rule times the earlier events, and does it permit this stall? Data: NGL IGS20 daily GNSS heights (SENG and GEVK to 2026-10-17, HS02 to 2026-05-02, AUSV), event dates from the IMO chronology. We removed a 50.7 cm antenna-height artefact at SENG. Method: leave-one-out tests of five trigger-rule families on the ten events, a stall test, and exponential versus exponential-plus-linear fits of the current recharge with block bootstrap. Results: (1) Re-inflation since the last floor is now 43.6 cm at SENG versus 24.8-31.7 cm before the five eruptions of May 2024-July 2025, and it passed the earlier maximum in March-April 2026 at SENG, GEVK and HS02 (IMO volumes give the same ratio). (2) A threshold that rises by 8.2 cm per event timed all ten onsets within 30 days but was passed on 2026-02-15; SENG is now 14 cm (3.5 SD) above it. A fixed re-inflation rule (similar to the IMO volume rule) was passed in November 2025. Rules that permit the stall because their threshold rises with time or needs fast loading (30-day fading memory) are rejected by the April and July 2025 eruptions; only fading memory of 90-180 days is not clearly rejected (median errors 24-34 days, stall margins 0.3-1.2 SD). (3) Recharge did not stop: a transient (tau about 90 days) plus a steady 16.9 cm/yr (15.8-17.9) at SENG fits much better than an exponential approach to a fixed level, at all four stations (bootstrap p <= 0.007). Limitations: ten events and one stall; rule families were chosen after the stall was known; uplift is only a proxy for reservoir pressure; no source modelling, InSAR or seismicity.

display.caption: Daily vertical position at SENG (antenna artefact removed) and HS02, October 2023 to the last data. Dotted lines: onsets of the 11 events. Circles: level on the day before each onset. Current cycle: exponential fit (green, dashed) and exponential plus steady term (orange). Dash-dot line: current floor plus the largest earlier re-inflation.

Re-inflation since each post-event floor for the cycles that ended in the May 2024 to July 2025 eruptions (blue, dot = onset of the next event) and for the current cycle (orange), at SENG, HS02 and GEVK.

Leave-one-out median onset timing error for ten events (x) versus the stall test z (y; above zero means the rule predicted an event that did not occur) for each trigger rule. Violet points: fading-memory rules with tau_r 7-365 days.
